subject: humanities
passage: Only a small fraction of the tragedies performed at the dramatic festivals of fifth-century BCE Athens has survived, and modern judgments about the genre therefore rest on a remarkably narrow foundation. Even for the three playwrights whose works were most carefully preserved, the losses are enormous. ______ Sophocles is thought to have written more than 120 plays, yet only seven survive complete, along with fragments of others, the longest of them part of a comic satyr play recovered from an Egyptian papyrus.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim: even for the best-preserved playwrights, "the losses are enormous." The last sentence gives one playwright, Sophocles, as a case of that claim: seven complete plays out of more than 120. A transition that introduces an illustration is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a new, separate point, but the figures about Sophocles do not add a new claim; they show how large the losses are. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "For instance" introduces Sophocles as a specific case of the enormous losses just described.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something true despite the previous point, but the survival of only seven plays confirms the losses rather than going against them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence does not restate the claim in other words; it moves from a general statement to particular numbers for one writer.
